CI VISIBILITY: SURFACE TEST FAILURES AND REVIEW LAB FAILURE CAUSES AS GITHUB ANNOTATIONS. Base on current origin/main (expected 3b6ee91; record the SHA you start from). New branch, no target branch.

WHY: reviewers who work through the GitHub REST API (no log or artifact download) can only see check-run annotations and step timings. Today a failing pytest step shows just 'Process completed with exit code 1', and a failing Review Lab step shows just 'Process completed with exit code 2' with a job summary that says only 'failed'. Two PRs are currently blocked because nobody can see WHICH test failed or WHAT the Review Lab error text was. GitHub turns any stdout line of the form '::error file=F,line=N,title=T::MESSAGE' into an annotation readable through the API.

ALLOWED FILES (any other changed path is a failure): tests/conftest.py, tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py (new), .github/workflows/review-lab.yml, CHANGES.md.

CHANGE 1 - tests/conftest.py. Add a pytest hook that emits one GitHub annotation per failed test, ONLY when os.environ.get('GITHUB_ACTIONS') == 'true'. Implement as:
(a) a pure helper `def github_failure_annotation(nodeid: str, location: tuple[str, int | None, str] | None, longrepr_text: str, when: str) -> str` that returns a single line '::error file=<relpath>,line=<line+1>,title=<when>: <nodeid>::<message>' where: relpath is the test file path from location[0] as given by pytest (already repo-relative), omitting ',line=...' when location[1] is None; message is longrepr_text with GitHub command escaping applied (replace '%' with '%25', '\r' with '%0D', '\n' with '%0A') and truncated to 1000 characters BEFORE escaping (append ' ...' when truncated); title escapes ',' as '%2C' and ':' as '%3A' per GitHub's property escaping. Also apply '%'->'%25', '\r'->'%0D', '\n'->'%0A' to the title. If longrepr_text is empty use 'see job log'.
(b) a hook `def pytest_runtest_logreport(report: pytest.TestReport) -> None` that returns immediately unless GITHUB_ACTIONS == 'true' and report.failed is True; builds longrepr_text as: for report.when == 'call' use `report.longreprtext` (fall back to str(report.longrepr)); for 'setup'/'teardown' the same but the title prefix is the phase name so errors in fixtures are distinguishable; then prints the annotation line with print(..., flush=True). Wrap the body in try/except Exception: pass so a formatting problem can never fail or hide a test. Cap at 50 annotations per session via a module-level counter (GitHub shows a limited number per step; emit a final single '::warning title=pytest annotations::more than 50 failures; see job log' when the cap is hit, once).
Do NOT change pytest_collection_modifyitems or the reset_rate_limiter_state fixture. Keep ruff clean (repo config, py314).

CHANGE 2 - tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py (new). Unit tests for the helper only (no GitHub needed): (1) a call-phase failure with location ('tests/test_x.py', 41, 'test_y') and a two-line longrepr produces exactly '::error file=tests/test_x.py,line=42,title=call%3A tests/test_x.py%3A%3Atest_y::AssertionError%3A boom%0Aassert 1 == 2' (compute the exact expected string from your implementation and assert it literally); (2) line omitted when location line is None; (3) '%' in the message becomes '%25' and the result contains no raw newline; (4) a 5000-char message is truncated to 1000 chars plus ' ...' before escaping; (5) empty longrepr gives 'see job log'; (6) the hook is a no-op when GITHUB_ACTIONS is unset: call pytest_runtest_logreport with a simple failed-report stand-in object (attributes failed=True, when='call', nodeid, location, longreprtext) under monkeypatch.delenv('GITHUB_ACTIONS', raising=False) and assert capsys captured nothing; (7) with monkeypatch.setenv('GITHUB_ACTIONS','true') the same stand-in produces exactly one line starting with '::error file='. Mark the module with pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit.

CHANGE 3 - .github/workflows/review-lab.yml, step 'Write Review Lab job summary' (the inline Python heredoc). Keep every existing summary line. Add, after the existing lines are built and only when report.get('ok') is not True: (a) summary lines '- Failure code: <report.get("failure_code") or "none">' and '- Failure summary: <first 800 chars of report.get("failure_summary") or "none", newlines replaced by " | ">'; (b) for each phase in report.get('phase_results', {}) whose status is 'failed', a summary line '- Phase <name>: failed (<failure_code>) <first 400 chars of summary>'; (c) GitHub annotations printed to stdout with print(..., flush=True): one '::error title=Review Lab failure::<failure_code>: <failure_summary truncated to 1000 chars>' and one '::error title=Review Lab phase <name>::<failure_code>: <summary truncated to 600 chars>' per failed phase, applying the same '%'->'%25', '\r'->'%0D', '\n'->'%0A' escaping to the message and '%'->'%25', ':'->'%3A', ','->'%2C' to the title. When the report pointer file does not exist, additionally print '::error title=Review Lab failure::no sanitised report was written (verify did not reach the report stage)'. These values come from the report that the workflow ALREADY uploads as a public artifact, so no new information is exposed; do not print environment variables, DSNs or the raw compose file. Do not change any other step. Keep the YAML valid (run `python -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/review-lab.yml'))"`).

CHANGE 4 - CHANGES.md: one new dated entry (2026-10-10) titled 'CI failure causes surfaced as GitHub annotations' with two or three sentences: failed pytest tests now emit ::error annotations with file, line, test id and the assertion text when running under GitHub Actions; the Review Lab job summary now shows the failure code, failure summary and failed phases, and emits them as annotations; nothing about test selection, assertions or gates changed.

VALIDATION (run all; paste the exact commands and pass/fail counts in your final message):
1. python -m pytest tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py tests/test_review_lab_v3.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
2. GITHUB_ACTIONS=true python -m pytest tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py -q -p no:cacheprovider   (must still pass; the hook only fires for failures)
3. Create a throwaway failing test file OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/annot_probe/test_probe.py with `def test_boom(): assert 1 == 2`), run `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider --rootdir=. -c pyproject.toml /tmp/annot_probe/test_probe.py -q` from the repo root and confirm stdout contains exactly one line starting with '::error file=' and containing 'test_boom'; then delete the throwaway file. Do not add it to the repo.
4. ruff check tests/conftest.py tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py
5. Full unit suite as CI runs it, must be 0 failures: CI=true CORS_ORIGINS=http://test EDDN_SIMULATION_INGEST_ENABLED=false PYTHONPATH=$PWD/apps/api/src python -m pytest --ignore=tests/integration --ignore=tests/test_deploy_main_invariants_gate.py -m "unit or not (integration or db or operator or e2e or slow)" -q -p no:cacheprovider
6. git diff --name-only origin/main lists only the four allowed paths.
Do NOT weaken, skip or delete any existing test or assertion. Commit message: 'ci: surface pytest failures and Review Lab failure causes as GitHub annotations'.
